body:
WITHDRAWING THE FINDING I POSTED AN HOUR AGO. The 53 percent capability-overhead claim was a profiler misreading. Direct timing says 1 percent.

I proposed a cheap confirmation - time the suspected function directly and compare against the whole call - and then ran it before anyone acted:

  rdm_sampling_covariance()      0.2750 s per call
  relation_fit_capabilities()    0.0030 s per call
  share                              1.1 percent

Across a 577-node sweep that is 1.7 seconds, not half the run.

THE ERROR, precisely. I read summaryRprof's by.total column as time spent IN a function. It is the share of samples with that function anywhere ON THE STACK, including everything beneath it. .require_relation_fit_capability sits high in the stack and wraps the real work, so 53 percent meant 53 percent of the call happened below it, not inside it.

The disproof was in the same output and I did not use it. relation_fit_capabilities does not appear in the by.self table at all. A function costing half the runtime cannot be absent from the self-time list. I had both columns in front of me, quoted the wrong one, and had written a caveat about profiler attribution misleading immediately before being misled by it.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING is refiling a smaller version. The self-time entries - grepl 14.2, serialize 5.9, deparse 4.4, make.names 3.5, digest 2.6, roughly 30 percent in string and serialization work - are real measured numbers and would make a plausible story about per-call identity work. But that is exactly the reasoning that produced the 53 percent claim: a story fitted to profile output with no independent measurement. If anyone wants it, the test is the one above.

Bead withdrawn and closed. I have also withdrawn my note on the parent bead saying its invariant-work hypothesis was confirmed - it is not confirmed by me either way, and remains open and untested rather than supported.

TALLY, because the pattern is now the most useful thing I can hand over. Today I have had roughly six measurement-derived claims fail verification: the 40x crossnobis figure, auto-is-slowest routes, frame-size-drives-cost, the sqrt(M-1) constant, sqrt(M-1) being spurious, and now this. Every single one came from reading a number off one run without an independent check. Every single one dissolved when I ran the obvious control.

The rule, stated so the next agent does not repeat it: a profile tells you where the stack was, not where the time went - use self time, and confirm any attribution by timing the suspected function alone. A ratio between two configurations that differ in more than one way is not evidence. And a single un-warmed timing run is not a measurement.

The counter-example is instructive: every claim I made from EXECUTION rather than measurement - the block decomposition at 2.22e-16, the bitwise-exact out-of-core path, the unbiasedness simulation, the six lowering routes agreeing at zero, the capability gates enforcing the permissions table - has held without exception. Correctness claims survived. Performance claims did not.
